At issue: "The compiled checker keeps the multiple instantiation exclusion rule."
Reports: "The exclusion rule is the type group's published position four times over … The [Working Draft's] own types chapter says the numeric types "are mutually exclusive; no value has more than one of them" (`types-vals-vars.tex:502`)" (judgement §2, tenet 5).
Plain: Missing: the 2011 paper (`exclusion.tick:141-152`), the 2012 Types chapter (`types.tick:355-376`), Naden 2012 (`justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497`), POPL 2019, that sentence.
Ground: those lines; on 2026-10-26 07:46:17 UTC he wrote "I think we did a plenty of digging which decided why we took the flat numeric tower." Elsewhere: F-44 (`TypeMapping.tex:125`, added in 0d2206c5f) and F-46; that sentence is in no FACTS or POSITIONS entry.

**P-48**, an unfixed type parameter takes its bound. Named: the judgement finds it is POPL 2019's own rule (§3). No fault found.

**P-58** (a), the reason.
At issue: "the library's own form, and it keeps that form"
Reports: "The entry's ground "the specification prints `builtinPrimitive`'s declaration" is weak: it is true only through the included library api, whose comment describes walk's mechanism" (judgement §2, tenet 8).
Plain: That ground was in the first text (2026-10-10, 046207371); the present text gives none. The form is outside the language, so the library's practice (all 424 bindings) decides.
Ground: `Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/future.tex:675`; `FortressBuiltin.fsi:14-29`; F-32; the judge's reasoning. Elsewhere: no.

At issue: the decision as a whole.
Reports: "the yes must be informed and must come before climb batch 23, since after 449 bindings move the other form costs a library sweep" (judgement §2, tenet 8).
Plain: Owed. On 2026-10-22 22:02:17 UTC he wrote "I don't recall my decision asking for static methods so I am unable to make fully informed decision from this fragment." None found to 2026-10-26 07:00 UTC.
Ground: his words. Elsewhere: BOOT.md ask 4; `reviews/phase3-exit/judgement.md` §1 item 5.

Reports: "P-59's "microGPT's static types are concrete" is the coordinator's premise, unmeasured (rq 221), measurable only when microGPT compiles" (judgement §2, tenet 9).
Plain: Reason not the curator's; unmeasured.
Ground: the coordinator's text of 2026-09-29 14:08:16 UTC, which he did not take up (evidence map, tenet 9(b)). Elsewhere: review-queue item 221, open.

Reports: "stamping "only renames", so no generic instance can hold a `double[]`; … "unboxing will build on" stamping. Both are [JVM] statements and both can be true (the class loader's way, A4, is unmeasured); the record must say so in one place" (judgement §2, tenet 7).

Reports: "His 09-20 lean for the class-loader way was "recorded as your leans, to confirm" and is in no entry" (judgement §2, tenet 7).

**P-26** (b), no source. At issue: "The implementers' later word also outweighs unfinished text."
Reports: "…is the coordinator's sentence with no source (review-queue item 215)" (judgement, tenet 2); strike it (judgement §9, item 4).
Plain: Reason not the curator's; nothing rests on it.
Ground: commit bc8902f47 (2026-09-30); positions audit, P-26 note §3. Elsewhere: review-queue item 215, open.

**P-26** (c), no test for "later". At issue: "The revival does not second-guess them: it knows less than they did."
Reports: "(4) date a code commit against the texts before calling it "later"; (5) where two later sources conflict, stop ranking and decide by P-8's goal, saying so" (judgement §7).

Ground: the judge's reasoning; trap grades §4; his yes to rewording P-26 and P-37, 2026-10-26 07:42:15 UTC. Elsewhere: no.

**P-27**, the library's practice. At issue: "The library's own practice is the standard."
Reports: "supplied Y's wrong-[layer] ground … P-27 governs how the library is extended … It does not decide between two of the team's own designs; the dated later word does" (trap grades §4; Y is the old reader).

Ground: trap test, scenario 2. Elsewhere: no.

**P-33**, the phase order. At issue: "reports no error on the interpreter's whole library"
Reports: ""The interpreter's whole library" is wider than F-53's twelve, and his 10-26 goal says "the fuller library". No step names the bound flip (F-289)." (judgement, tenet 6).
Plain: The zero covers twelve components (fourteen with `List`'s imports); the other 38 block P-12's step; code generation was unmeasured (F-34).
Ground: F-53, F-290, F-289, F-34; his words of 2026-10-26 04:47:50 and 07:30:36 UTC; dialogue §9. Elsewhere: those FACTS; BOOT.md ask 3.

**P-37** (a), his reason is missing. At issue: "as a bootstrap to remove"
Reports: "His goal of 10-26 … is the [language] reason and is not in the entry" (judgement, tenet 3).
Plain: Missing reason; the old reader listed a `CompilerSystem` bridge (scenario 4: 1 of 2).
Ground: his words, 2026-10-26 04:47:50 UTC: "The whole point of the switchover is to avoid the need to port walks library into the compilers library." Elsewhere: dialogue §4 only.

**P-37** (b), a permission with no rule. At issue: "the one library may take a design of the prelude's"
Reports: "this reads an [JVM-layer] bootstrap as a design source with no rule for when" (judgement, tenet 3).
Plain: Missing rule; judgement §3 gives it (the team's later language text, or its checker enforcing the design; never a stub; "later" is a date).
Ground: the judge's reasoning; his caution of 2026-10-26 07:30:36 UTC. Old reader: scenario 2, 1 of 2. Elsewhere: designs that do not bind: F-84, F-225; the rule: no.

**P-37** (c), the premise. At issue: "the compiled path reads the interpreter's library with it"
Reports: "So the premise is unmeasured, not refuted. … F-34 and [the phase 3 exit judgement's] two phase-4 zeros are now the answer, and the entry should carry it" (judgement, tenet 3).
Plain: The library is shown to check, not to run, compiled.
Ground: F-34 (52 refusals), rows 339 and 832; his doubt of 2026-09-20 15:18:35 UTC. Elsewhere: F-34, F-291, those rows; the entry: no.

**P-37** (d), three files. At issue: "its own library files `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin` and `CompilerAlgebra`"
Reports: "names three files, so that `CompilerSystem` falls outside its letter" (trap key, scenario 4).
Plain: A fourth wired file, `CompilerSystem`, is imported by 27 compiled tests.
Ground: prelude sweep §0; `reviews/phase3-exit/zero-audit.md` A.2. Elsewhere: no.

**P-38**, the prelude's defects go with it. Named as a cross-reference of P-37.

**P-42** (a), "functions". At issue: "`Any` holds tuples, functions and `()`, which `Object` does not."
Reports: ""Functions" (review-queue item 218): the [Working Draft] puts arrows outside `Object`, the Types chapter inside; drop the word" (judgement §4).
Plain: The texts disagree on functions, agree on tuples and `()`; his yes rested on the tuples.
Ground: `types-vals-vars.tex:136`, `:215-216` against `types.tick:232-238`; his yes 2026-09-29 14:02:25 UTC. Elsewhere: review-queue item 218, open.

**P-42** (b), the departure. At issue: "which ends the departure"
Reports: "the switch-over ends nothing by itself; `Shell.java:372` does, and no step named it (F-289, 685 errors under the command's setting)" (judgement §4).
Plain: False: one line holds `Object`; no plan step flips it. `()` and a tuple-typed dotted method fail under either bound.
Ground: `Shell.java:371-386`; Steele's 91e71e62e, c61723f61, afb02f41d (2012-05-28 to 30). Elsewhere: F-289, F-291, rows 412, 339, 832 (0d2206c5f); rung B of climb batch 22c.

**P-42** (c), grounds missing. At issue: "The specification states the bound `Any`, with a callout"
Reports: "(1) cite POPL 2019, the [Working Draft's] instantiation sentence and the library's practice as the grounds" (judgement §7).
Plain: Missing reasons. POPL 2019: "By default, each type parameter has an upper bound Any".
Ground: `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019.txt:418-419`; `trait-parameters.tex:53-54`. Elsewhere: no.

**P-42** (d), a stale example. At issue: "its arrays indexed by pairs, such as `(ZZ32,ZZ32)`, are among them"
Reports: "Since P-156, the arrays' index parameter has an explicit bound `Index`, so P-42's example "arrays indexed by pairs" no longer rests on the implicit bound" (evidence map, tenet 4(c)).
Plain: False as an example; element types such as `(E,F)` still rest on it.
Ground: P-156's text; `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:759`, `:1364`. Elsewhere: no.

**P-43** (a), two reasons not his. At issue: "the flattened prelude is the team's last record of the Fortress way"; "not how a specialisation is chosen"
Reports: his phrase "the team's last record" "was about the forest rule"; the second sentence "joins the two meanings of specialisation and he said it was not an answer" (judgement, tenet 5).
Plain: Reasons not his; wrong layer and date (2009 code, earlier than the texts).
Ground: his words 2026-09-24 01:02:52 UTC (of the forest rule; "Which clearly isn't an answer to the question") and 14:41:40 ("Agreed. Route A it is.", no reason). Elsewhere: review-queue items 219, 220, open.

**P-43** (b), the language's grounds. At issue: "The compiled checker keeps the multiple instantiation exclusion rule."
Reports: "The exclusion rule is the type group's published position four times over … numeric types "are mutually exclusive; no value has more than one of them" (`types-vals-vars.tex:502`)" (judgement, tenet 5).
Plain: Missing reasons: the 2011 paper, the 2012 Types chapter, Naden 2012, POPL 2019, that sentence.
Ground: `exclusion.tick:141-152`; `types.tick:355-376`; `justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497`; his words of 2026-10-26 07:46:17 UTC ("which decided why we took the flat numeric tower"). Elsewhere: F-44, F-46 (`TypeMapping.tex:125` added in 0d2206c5f); the sentence is in no FACTS or POSITIONS entry.

**P-44**, `AnyIntegral` stays closed. Named as a use of 2012 texts as the later word.

**P-47**, each integer type's own `MIN`, `MAX`. Named as rightly taken from the prelude.

**P-48**, an unfixed type parameter takes its bound. Named: it is POPL 2019's own rule (judgement §3).

**P-58** (a), the reason. At issue: "the library's own form, and it keeps that form"
Reports: "The entry's ground "the specification prints `builtinPrimitive`'s declaration" is weak: it is true only through the included library api" (judgement, tenet 8).
Plain: That ground was in the first text (2026-10-10, 046207371); the present text gives none. The form lies outside the language; the library's practice decides.
Ground: `Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/future.tex:675`; `FortressBuiltin.fsi:14-29`; F-32. Elsewhere: no.

**P-58** (b), his informed yes. At issue: the decision as a whole.
Reports: "the yes must be informed and must come before climb batch 23, since after 449 bindings move the other form costs a library sweep" (judgement, tenet 8).
Plain: Owed. On 2026-10-22 22:02:17 UTC he wrote "I don't recall my decision asking for static methods so I am unable to make fully informed decision from this fragment."
Ground: his words. Elsewhere: BOOT.md ask 4; `reviews/phase3-exit/judgement.md` §1 item 5.

**P-59**, walk's coercions. At issue: "MicroGPT's static types are concrete, each the type of the value itself and not a trait above it"
Reports: "P-59's "microGPT's static types are concrete" is the coordinator's premise, unmeasured (rq 221), measurable only when microGPT compiles" (judgement, tenet 9).
Plain: Reason not the curator's; unmeasured.
Ground: the coordinator's text of 2026-09-29 14:08:16 UTC, not taken up by him (evidence map, tenet 9(b)). Elsewhere: review-queue item 221, open.

**P-60**, `comprises` as values. Named in the prelude sweep.

**P-66**, the integer principle. Named in the prelude sweep.

**P-68**, float `floor` and `round`. Named in the prelude sweep.

**P-74**, mixed integer widths. Named in the prelude sweep and evidence map lists.

**P-75**, `NN32` into `RR64`. Named once (dialogue §6) as an earlier open ask, "P-75 withdrawn".

**P-76**, `IntLiteral`. Named as taken from the prelude.

**P-77**, ranges over `ZZ32`. The trap key lists its Why ("A range over another integer type is a static error.") and title as sentences that could mislead (scenarios 1, 3); no reader was misled (trap grades §4).

**P-78**, `SUM` and `PROD`. Named in the prelude sweep.

**P-80**, sign-refined types. Named in evidence map lists.

**P-84**, the `double[]` store. At issue: "decision A, how an `RR64` array made through the library's generic array traits gets that store"
Reports: "stamping "only renames", so no generic instance can hold a `double[]` … the class loader's way, A4, is unmeasured; the record must say so in one place" (judgement, tenet 7).
Plain: Missing: stamping alone gives no `double[]` field; way A4 is unmeasured; also the unboxing words of P-17.
Ground: `coordinator/array-design.md` §2, probe 1; `reviews/array-design-ways.md` §3. Elsewhere: F-18 (0d2206c5f).

**P-85**, the open array questions. At issue: "the array decisions A, B and D"
Reports: "His 09-20 lean for the class-loader way was "recorded as your leans, to confirm" and is in no entry" (judgement, tenet 7).
Plain: Missing: his lean of 2026-09-20, as a lean to confirm.
Ground: the coordinator's text of 2026-09-20 14:34:56 UTC: "Recorded as your leans, to confirm: for the unboxed store, the team's own direction, the class loader". Elsewhere: no.

**P-95**, specification changes recorded. Named as the place to weigh a return to route C (judgement §7).

**P-98**, `TotalComparison` and `StandardMinMax`. Named in the prelude sweep.

**P-146** (a), a reason that misleads. At issue: "Why: the checker reads the library as the team wrote it"
Reports: ""Why: the checker reads the library as the team wrote it" invited the reviewer's ground" (trap grades §4).
Plain: The old reader took it with P-27 to drop the prelude's `comprises T` because the library never had it. The ground is the date: Naden 2012-08-31 follows Steele's June 2012 edits.
Ground: trap test, scenario 2 (1 of 2); `justificationOfRTR.tex:626-630`. Elsewhere: no.

**P-146** (b), the idiom's history. At issue: nothing in the text; its ground.
Reports: "the history of the self-type idiom that P-146 rests on misses the team's last edit of that trait" (prelude sweep §7).
Plain: Steele added `comprises T` (655e65d53, 2012-06-05) and removed the F-bound (59fdeff62, 2012-06-06); the history ended 2011-12-06.
Ground: the two commits. Elsewhere: F-225 (0d2206c5f).

**P-147**, objects define abstract methods by covering bodies. Named in the prelude sweep.

**P-149**, a sibling's body does not define an abstract method. Named in the prelude sweep.

**P-152**, exclusion by existential reduction. Named as a language text used as the later word; review-queue item 228 (open) asks about its reason.

**P-153**, the integer power. At issue: "Why: the team's later code gives an integer power the type of its integer base at a signed exponent"
Reports: "its sound ground is that the [Working Draft's] ℚ-valued power was never built on either path and the prelude's rule is the only implemented one" (judgement §3).
Plain: Wrong layer: compiled-path code called the language's later word.
Ground: the judge's reasoning; prelude sweep, row P5 (5ad4a9957). Elsewhere: no; the rewrite note lists it as owed.

**P-154**, list order. At issue: "`Library/incomplete/advanced/Fortress.PartialTotalOrders.fss:117-140`"
Reports: "a library draft whose first commit in git is the root snapshot `5a68404fd`, 2012-07-19, so its date is unknown" (evidence map, tenet 2(c)).
Plain: "Later" cannot be shown for this draft. Ground: git. Elsewhere: no.

**P-155**, symbolic operators. At issue: "The compiled checker checks the overloads of symbolic operators before the switch-over."
Reports: "Row 782: the export check reads top-level symbolic operators (P-155 read to cover the export check …)" (judgement §5, rung 2).
Plain: The entry speaks of the overloading check; the batch reads it as covering the export check. His yes is open.
Ground: dialogue §6; row 782. Elsewhere: BOOT.md ask 1; climb batch 22c, question 2; F-287.

**P-156**, `Index`. Named as the reason P-42's example is stale (P-42 (d)).

**P-157**, vectors stay additive groups. Named in the prelude sweep; its reasons are not re-ruled (judgement §3).

**P-158** (a), the specification. At issue: "The specification asks for no body there, not for no declaration"
Reports: ""for each field declaration and non-abstract method declaration in the exported declaration", and may give an abstract one a concrete declaration (`Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:372-385`" (rewrite note).
Plain: False: the export rule asks no declaration for an abstract member. P-158 rests on the team's later export check (P-26). Judgement §3 had called the text unclear.
Ground: those lines; the team's checker quoted the rule in 80d8c678a (2009-02-03). Elsewhere: climb batch 22c, question 3; BOOT.md ask 2.

**P-158** (b), the date. At issue: "the team's export check of 2012 enforces it"
Reports: "the count is Sukyoung Ryu's, `ac0d41de0`, 2009-05-08; `5a68404fd` and `a9c625b1e` of 2012 are parentless snapshots" (rewrite note, "Still owed").
Plain: False date: the member count is of 2009-05-08.
Ground: commit ac0d41de0 (sukyoungryu). Elsewhere: row 816 (60aaeb6bb); the entry: no.

interpreter reads the bound so.

has an upper bound Any'' (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, POPL 2019).

declarations the bound \TYP{Object} (row~412 of the revival's gap ledger), a
divergence that lasts until the compiled path is switched over to the
